body.text: In-vessel drops are modeled as an instantaneous release of the inventory from all pins in one or two high burnup assemblies.
body.anchor: an instantaneous release of the radionuclide inventory from all pins in one high burnup fuel assembly

body.text: Radionuclides leave the primary functional containment boundary at an assumed one percent of cover gas volume per day.
body.anchor: assumed rate of one percent of cover gas volume per day

body.text: The SFP drop is assumed 310 days after the assembly is stored in In-Vessel Storage.
body.anchor: is assumed to occur 310 days after the fuel assembly is stored

body.text: When cladding is damaged in the pool, the fuel pin sodium bond reacts with water in an exothermic gas-producing reaction.

body.text: The analysis therefore uses a reduced pool decontamination factor for that particulate.

body.text: The FHB volume is assumed to exhaust instantaneously with no credit for NHV filtration.
